To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neural networks allow to simulate efficiently even anisotropic elastic-plastic deformations of foam structures with anisotropic damage and non-associated plasticity.

neural networks are a powerful tool to model the constitutive behavior, even for complex irreversible materials like foam structures, if the neural network is trained with the help of a hybrid multi scale method.

neural networks can be successfully embedded into the established framework rate independent plasticity, and that this hybrid approach can be applied for the simulation of anisotropic damage and plastic deformation in foam structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new hybrid multi-scale neural network approach (HMNNA) to describe the homogenized anisotropic elastic-plastic behavior of foams.
the development of a hybrid multi-scale approach to simulate the irreversible behavior of foams.
a novel hybrid approach that allows to efficiently simulate the irreversible anisotropic plastic deformation and damage of foamed materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed HyMNNA approach is a very promising alternative to classical phenomenological and computational homogenization approaches, in particular for complex irreversible mechanisms.
the HyMNNA is a promising approach to simulate the anisotropic homogenized elastic plastic deformations of foams with coupled anisotropy of damage and non-associative plasticity.
the HyMNNA approach is able to capture complex material behavior in the framework of rate-independent plasticity, while keeping the computational effort of the simulation at a low level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neural networks are very well suited for constitutive modeling of irreversible material behavior.
the presented HyMNNA approach allows the efficient simulation of the anisotropic irreversible elastic plastic behavior of complex micro structures.
we have developed a novel hybrid neural network method for the simulation of the anisotropic irreversible elastic plastic deformation and damage behavior of foams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HyMNNA approach is capable of predicting the complex anisotropic elastic-plastic behavior of foam structures in an efficient way.
the proposed hybrid neural network approach is a promising way to efficiently simulate the anisotropic plastic and damage behavior of foam materials, even under multi scale loading.
neural networks can be embedded in established frameworks of plasticity and damage, which is of great advantage for practical applications.
